items.title: The spectral gap of a projection scan is at most its modified gap, which is at most the square root of n times the gap
items.author: Jason Gaitonde; Elchanan Mossel
items.work: Spectral independence, coupling and mixing times of projection scans
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 396-402: for a finite product space with a projection scan whose transition matrix is the product of the coordinate matrices, the spectral gap is at most the modified gap, which is at most the square root of n times the spectral gap. The proof (source lines 403-433) has two parts of different kinds: the first inequality is obtained by testing the quadratic form on a mean-zero unit-variance function and applying the reverse triangle inequality, which isolates one factor of the product, while the second is a comparison of the modified gap with the Dirichlet form of a single coordinate step, where the square root of the number of coordinates appears. The statement records neither the test-function step nor the Dirichlet-form computation.
